verses.uthmani: بِّسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ
verses.saheeh: By the fig and the olive
verses.khattab: By the fig and the olive ˹of Jerusalem˺
verses.jalalayn: By the fig and the olive, that is, the two [edible] foods — or [these denote the names of] two mountains in Syria on which these two foods grow —
verses.romanUrdu: Kasam hai Injir(fig) ki aur Zaitun ki

verses.jalalayn: and [by] the Mount Sinai, the mountain on which God, exalted be He, spoke to Moses (sīnīn means ‘the one blessed’ or ‘the fair one with fruitful trees’),
and [by] this secure land: Mecca, as people were secure in it in the time of pagandom and [are still secure in it] in Islam.

verses.uthmani: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍۢ
verses.indopak: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا الۡاِنۡسَانَ فِىۡۤ اَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيۡمٍ
verses.transliteration: Laqad khalaqnal insaana fee ahsani taqweem
verses.saheeh: We have certainly created man in the best of stature;
verses.khattab: Indeed, We created humans in the best form
verses.jalalayn: Verily We created man (al-insān: the generic) in the best of forms, [in the best] proportioning of his shape.
verses.romanUrdu: Humne Insan ko behtarin saakht par paida kiya

verses.transliteration: Thumma ra dad naahu asfala saafileen
verses.saheeh: Then We return him to the lowest of the low,
verses.khattab: But We will reduce them to the lowest of the low ˹in Hell˺
verses.jalalayn: Then, in the case of certain individuals of his [species], We reduced him to the lowest of the low — a metaphor for old age and weakness, at which point a believer’s deeds are fewer than when he was young; but he will still have his reward, as God, exalted be He, says:
verses.romanUrdu: Phir usey ulta pher kar humne sab neechon se neech kar diya

verses.uthmani: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍۢ
verses.indopak: اِلَّا الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا وَعَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ فَلَهُمۡ اَجۡرٌ غَيۡرُ مَمۡنُوۡنٍ ؕ
verses.transliteration: Ill-lal lazeena aamanoo wa 'amilus saalihaati; falahum ajrun ghairu mamnoon
verses.saheeh: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted.
verses.khattab: except those who believe and do good—they will have a never-ending reward
verses.jalalayn: except those who believe and perform righteous deeds, for they shall have an unfailing reward, one unending — in a hadīth [it is stated], ‘When a believer reaches that stage of old age which prevents him from performing [good] deeds, then what he used to do is recorded in his favour [instead]’.
verses.romanUrdu: Siwaye un logon ke jo iman laye aur neik amal karte rahey kay unke liye kabhi khatam na hone wala ajar hai

verses.transliteration: Fama yu kaz zibuka b'adu bid deen
verses.saheeh: So what yet causes you to deny the Recompense?
verses.khattab: Now, what makes you deny the ˹final˺ Judgment
verses.jalalayn: So what makes you deny, O disbeliever, thereafter — after the mention of man being created in the best of forms and his being reduced to the vilest of age, all of which indicates the power [of God] to resurrect — the Judgement?, the Requital that will be preceded by the Resurrection and the Reckoning. In other words, what makes you disbelieve in all this? Nothing does!
verses.romanUrdu: Pas (aey nabi) iske baad kaun jaza o saza ke maamle mei tumko jhutla sakta hai

verses.saheeh: Is not Allah the most just of judges?
verses.khattab: Is Allah not the most just of all judges
verses.jalalayn: Is not God the fairest of all judges?, the most just of all judges. His passing judgement by means of [the process of] requital is one such example. In a hadīth [it is stated], ‘Whoever recites [sūrat] wa’l-tīni, ‘By the fig’, to the end of it, let him then say, “Yes Indeed! And I am of those who bear witness to this!” ’
verses.romanUrdu: Kya Allah sab hakimon se bada hakim nahin hai
